[h1] The Big Picture [/h1]
I'm speechless really, despite selling 40 million copies and being 95% recommended, this is genuinely one of the most ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ survival games I ever played. I can't recall a single game in the genre, that I have ever played, that isn't better in just about every category. I have a lot of hours of hosting the world for friends, and I wanted to see it through to the end, but every time I played it, I was just thinking I had to get further before it got fun. That moment never came. I'm left here grappling with what the hell 40 million people see in this game that I, after 90 hours, could not. There is almost nothing positive I can say about this game.

[h1] Let's talk about the world and art direction [/h1]
The world is hideous, generic, and in most places, copy-pasted. It looks like an asset flip, frankly. There is no cohesive art direction that ties the game together or gives it a signature look. The world art clashes heavily with the cartoony style of pals. The graphics are very poor from a technical standpoint but also there is no post processing or anything being done to the final image to create any kind of tone or art style. There's no music, like anywhere, in the entire game, except for generic combat music and combat sounds. There's almost no ambient sound at all, period. I was constantly thinking my game had lost audio while playing, because it's just dead silent outside of combat. It lacks any sense of level design, and what attempt at level design there is, is invalidated by flying mounts. You'd think maybe there'd be some good level design in one of the many, many dungeons, but no. The dungeons are literally all completely identical sets of the same couple rooms and a random boss at the end. And even those copy pasted rooms, are just rooms, there is nothing interesting happening in any of them. Pals aimlessly wander the world waiting to be killed like an MMO.

[h1] Combat is Ok but still not a strength [/h1]
The combat was serviceable but very buggy. The more impressive the game tries to be, like world bosses and arenas, the buggier and more unplayable it gets. After a point, the entire game devolved into rotating through sets of laser-firing pals on cooldown. The bigger the game tries to go (world bosses, arena combat), the more dysfunctional and unplayable it gets. The difficulty is unbelievably easy, and basically anything hard in the game can easily be cheesed by just recalling your pals when the enemy tries to attack them. 

[h1] Not for players who enjoy crafting [/h1]
The building is the worst building I have ever seen in this genre, period. Not only are the blocks hideous, large, and uncustomizeable, but the base building space is drastically too small, and the pals just clip through everything so badly that you will generally not even be able to see what is happening or where you are going in your base at most times. In terms of story, there is no story. Material gathering is unnecessarily grindy,  and worse, real time crafting times on items are egregiously long and have no gameplay justification whatsoever and cannot be disabled in server options. The game falls into the Starbound trap of pretending to have a ton of things to craft but really they are all just the same couple of items you start with but with an unjustifiable number of tiers to go through, where the only difference is their numbers and they have no effect on gameplay.

[h1] final thoughts [/h1]
There is nothing of substance happening here. The only thing, the ONLY thing, this game has going for it, is the pokemon gimmick. And apparently that alone is enough to make one of the worst made games in the survival crafting genre sell 40 million copies and get 95% on steam. Now if you'll excuse me, I'm going to go see how to get myself Twilight Zoned back to the real world where terrible games aren't worshipped by millions.

It's fun. Movement controls feel very good, the map is packed with creatures to capture, dungeons, loot, bosses and schematics to find.

My two biggest complaints about the game:
1)  Automation is severely lacking; you spend way too long having to manually queue up intermediary components
2)  The last 20% of the technology tree gets super grindy; and then once you get into the final area, all the previous resource grinds become instantly trivial, but it's replaced with a new resource grind that you can't ignore, because it replaces all you gear with new best-in-slot weapons/armor.

Well worth the price if you enjoy sandbox building/exploration game.  There's not a lot of 'survival' elements here; and it's not hard to find places you can put your base so that you *never* get raided, but the exploration is genuinely fun.

Absolute waste of money. This game is unfinished and unbalanced as hell. If you do waste money buying this ♥♥♥♥, here's some tips. 
Don't play any servers where you drop stuff on death and if you're playing solo, turn off dropping items on death. You will be dying constantly to stupid unavoidable attacks. Enemies can laser you with attacks that home in on you and stop you from moving as well as sucking you into the attack, and they can do this through several stories and multiple walls. You will not beat anything unless you're 40 levels higher than it and even then it will be a difficult fight. 
Do not bother with summoning bosses at the altar. They give ♥♥♥♥ for rewards and can't be defeated until you're at least 50 levels higher than they are. 
Don't bother with weapons until you get the Vortex Beater. All other weapons do laughable amounts of damage and reloading takes ages. 
Be sure if you're playing solo to turn food decay off, because there is no purpose to the decay besides forcing you to place more pals at your base to keep the food cool. You'll eventually be making so much food so rapidly that it won't matter if you have decay on or not.
Turn raids off. They don't provide any value or fun. They're just annoying.
Don't buy any gear or weapon blueprints. You'll find those for free out in the world and at better quality, too.
